subject: POC: routing policy hands-on — availability sweep & regional model shortlist
messages:
From: Alexis Moreno <alexis.moreno@acme-health.com>

Cc: Samir Patel <samir@finapps.io>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 14:08:00 -0400
Subject: POC kickoff — hands-on session request and availability

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We discussed a hands-on POC session to validate routing behavior across regions and a short load test on representative prompts. Our engineering and product leads are keen to get a concrete slot in the next two weeks.

Key asks for the session: 
- 90-minute working session (prompt review, routing rules, failover exercise, short load test)
- Confirmation of model variants you recommend for US/EU tiers
- A brief prework checklist so our infra team can open firewall rules and share sample datasets

Who will attend from your side? For scheduling, we have availability Mar 30–Apr 1 in the afternoons (ET). Let me know a few slots and any prep we should do.

Alexis
Alexis Moreno
Director of Product, Acme Health
alexis.moreno@acme-health.com

Alexis — great to hear. We can run the 90-minute lab and include a 10–15 minute quickload to validate routing and fallback tiers. From our side: myself (session lead), Rishi (inference/runtime), and Lauren (ops/load testing).

Proposed slots (ET):
- Tue Mar 30 14:00–15:30 ET
- Wed Mar 31 15:00–16:30 ET
- Thu Apr 1 13:00–14:30 ET

I'll attach a short prework checklist and the regional model shortlist — please share firewall/IPs and a sample prompt set (10–20 prompts) ahead of time.

Also tagging Rishi: Rishi, for the load test we should be explicit about target QPS and sequence lengths (Acme mentioned batch inference for summary workflows). Any preferences on quantized variants to try first?

Thanks,
Mina

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 26 Mar 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — hands-on session request and availability

Thanks — quick technical notes from my side:
- For US production-like routing: recommend trying model-v2.1 (FP16) and model-v2.1-q4 for cost/latency comparison.
- For EU: model-eu-v1 (lower token cost) and fallback to model-v2.1-q4 if latency SLOs fail.
- For the load test: if you can provide 20 representative prompts, I'll script a 5-minute ramp to target 50 requests/sec (burst to 75) to exercise batching and prefix cache.

I'll add a short spreadsheet with model recommendations — naming it regional-model-shortlist.xlsx. Can you confirm whether the PII sample prompts will be redacted, or if we should run with tokenized placeholders?

—Rishi
